greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who calls us to be children of the light, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you have entrusted us with the gift of life and the light of your truth. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you call us to be faithful in the small things and generous in our love. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you promise that those who trust in you will share in your master's joy. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed are those who fear the Lord.
homily:
We begin today with a very small, very familiar image: the act of holding a key. Think of the keys you carry in your pocket or your purse—the ones for your front door, the ones for your car, the ones that unlock the places where you belong. A key is a promise of access. It is a small piece of metal that says, 'You are expected here. You have a place to return to. You are not an outsider.' We carry these keys without thinking, trusting that when we reach the end of our day, the lock will turn, the door will open, and we will find ourselves back in the warmth of home. There is a profound, quiet security in having a key. It is the physical proof that we are anchored to a place and to people who know our name.

I want you to hold onto this image: the key. It is the image of a life that is entrusted with something precious. It is the image of Benjamin Vo. Think of his brilliant, searching mind—the boy who could effortlessly master 8th-grade math while still in the 4th grade, the boy who coded games and applications on GitHub, the boy who looked at the world with such boundless, intelligent curiosity. Whether he was exploring the intricacies of cloud infrastructure or simply sharing a laugh with his brother Ryan, Benjamin was a boy who understood that life is a series of opportunities—a series of talents—to be used, to be explored, and to be shared with love. He was a boy who held the keys to many hearts, and he used them to open doors of kindness and joy wherever he went.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: it has been five months since he went home to God. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know that the calendar moves forward, but the heart often stays in that room, in that moment, in that memory. We know the sharp, sudden ache that comes when you see something he would have loved—a new jet design, a complex math problem, a simple, silly joke—and the silence that follows is deafening. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the waves of sorrow that ambush you on a Tuesday morning. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame for the randomness of the world’s suffering. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus tells the parable of the talents, where a master entrusts his possessions to his servants. He gives them each a portion, not to hoard, but to multiply. To the one who uses what he has been given, the master says, 'Well done, my good and faithful servant. Come, share your master's joy.' This is the hinge of the whole mystery. We often think of our lives as things we must protect, things we must keep safe from the world. But Jesus tells us that life is a talent—a gift—that is meant to be spent in love. Benjamin lived this. Think of that remarkable moment when he, at just fifteen years old and completely unprompted, told his parents he was willing to give up his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William. He didn't need to break it open; the offer itself revealed the magnificent generosity of his soul. He was a boy whose heart was already sized for eternity. He was a boy who knew that the true wealth of life is not what we keep, but what we are willing to offer for the sake of those we love. That love is the talent that does not die; it is the gift that multiplies in the eyes of God.

Consider the first reading from Proverbs: 'When one finds a worthy wife, her value is far beyond pearls... She reaches out her hands to the poor, and extends her arms to the needy.' This reading speaks of the wisdom of a life lived for others, a life that is built upon the fear of the Lord. Benjamin walked in that wisdom. He walked in the truth of his gentle, respectful spirit. He walked in the truth of his empathy for his family. He walked in the truth of his joy. When you think of him, do not look for the complexity of the world or the mystery of his passing. Look for the truth of his life. Look for the way he smiled when he talked about his ‘con chim airlines’—that dream of a company that would take flight, that would soar. He found joy in the small, unexpected moments of life. He was a risk-taker in joy, a boy who embraced the adventure of being alive. That love is still flowing. It flows in the clean water of the well dedicated in his name in Cà Mau, bringing life to those in need. It flows in the quiet memories shared by everyone who knew his gentle spirit. His love did not stop when he crossed the threshold; it continues to work in the world, quietly and persistently.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart.

We hear in the Psalm today: 'Blessed are you who fear the LORD, who walk in his ways! ... Your children like olive plants around your table.' This is the turn of the heart. The blessing of the Lord is not that we will never suffer, but that we will never be abandoned in our suffering. Benjamin is now resting in that promise. He is dwelling in the land of the living, fully alive, fully healed, and fully embraced by the Father. He is not a memory tucked away in a photo album; he is a living soul in the Banquet of Heaven, standing alongside kindred spirits, watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. Think of the dream Alan had, where Ben and his dad stood outside room 419, and Ben said with that earnest voice, 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was the assurance that he has passed every test, that he is whole, and that he is watching over you with a smile. He is the one who has already crossed the threshold into the light, and he is cheering you on.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain overnight, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, only the clear, bright presence of God. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain. He is a light in the world, and he is shining for you. He is home. And because he is home, you are never truly lost. He is holding the key to that reunion, and he is waiting for the day when the family of four is whole again in the house of the Father.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For Benjamin Vo and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the light of Christ and share in the joy of the Master.
For all who are grieving, especially Alan, Thao, and Ryan, that God may console them with His peace and strengthen them with the hope of a future reunion.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
When one finds a worthy wife,
her value is far beyond pearls.
Her husband, entrusting his heart to her,
has an unfailing prize.
She brings him good, and not evil,
all the days of her life.
She obtains wool and flax
and works with loving hands.
She puts her hands to the distaff,
and her fingers ply the spindle.
She reaches out her hands to the poor,
and extends her arms to the needy.
Charm is deceptive and beauty fleeting;
the woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
Give her a reward for her labors,
and let her works praise her at the city gates.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (cf. 1a) Blessed are those who fear the Lord.
Blessed are you who fear the LORD,
who walk in his ways!
For you shall eat the fruit of your handiwork;
blessed shall you be, and favored.
R. Blessed are those who fear the Lord.
Your wife shall be like a fruitful vine
in the recesses of your home;
Your children like olive plants
around your table.
R. Blessed are those who fear the Lord.
Behold, thus is the man blessed
who fears the LORD.
The LORD bless you from Zion:
may you see the prosperity of Jerusalem
all the days of your life.
R. Blessed are those who fear the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 2
readings.text:
Concerning times and seasons, brothers and sisters,
you have no need for anything to be written to you. 
For you yourselves know very well that the day of the Lord will come
like a thief at night.
When people are saying, "Peace and security, "
then sudden disaster comes upon them,
like labor pains upon a pregnant woman,
and they will not escape.

But you, brothers and sisters, are not in darkness,
for that day to overtake you like a thief. 
For all of you are children of the light
and children of the day.
We are not of the night or of darkness. 
Therefore, let us not sleep as the rest do,
but let us stay alert and sober.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus told his disciples this parable:
"A man going on a journey
called in his servants and entrusted his possessions to them.
To one he gave five talents; to another, two; to a third, one--
to each according to his ability.
Then he went away.
Immediately the one who received five talents went and traded with them,
and made another five.
Likewise, the one who received two made another two.
But the man who received one went off and dug a hole in the ground
and buried his master's money.

"After a long time
the master of those servants came back
and settled accounts with them.
The one who had received five talents came forward
bringing the additional five.
He said, 'Master, you gave me five talents.
See, I have made five more.'
His master said to him, 'Well done, my good and faithful servant.
Since you were faithful in small matters,
I will give you great responsibilities.
Come, share your master's joy.'
Then the one who had received two talents also came forward and said,
'Master, you gave me two talents.
See, I have made two more.'
His master said to him, 'Well done, my good and faithful servant.
Since you were faithful in small matters,
I will give you great responsibilities.
Come, share your master's joy.'
Then the one who had received the one talent came forward and said,
'Master, I knew you were a demanding person,
harvesting where you did not plant
and gathering where you did not scatter;
so out of fear I went off and buried your talent in the ground.
Here it is back.'
His master said to him in reply, 'You wicked, lazy servant!
So you knew that I harvest where I did not plant
and gather where I did not scatter?
Should you not then have put my money in the bank
so that I could have got it back with interest on my return?
Now then! Take the talent from him and give it to the one with ten.
For to everyone who has,
more will be given and he will grow rich;
but from the one who has not,
even what he has will be taken away.
And throw this useless servant into the darkness outside,
where there will be wailing and grinding of teeth.'"

Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
